title: Allocator and Observability Unification Roadmap Q1 2027 - Q4 2028
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This roadmap describes a two-year program to unify the platform allocator (tenant placement, priority batching and soft quotas) with the observability surface (SLI/telemetry, dashboards and alerting flows). The goal is to reduce incidents caused by allocation-telemetry mismatch, improve operator mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) for token-latency incidents, and enable automated corrective actions (soft rebalancing, prefetch hints) without manual operator intervention.

Scope
-----
- Systems: allocator service (allocator-v2), placement-controller, prefetch-hint service, KV prefix cache sharder.
- Observability: telemetry-fanout, SLI synthesizer, token-cost-attribution pipeline, incident-explainability dashboards.
- Operator surface: new dashboard templates, runbooks, alert-suppression heuristics, and an SDK for building corrective playbooks.
- Excludes: hardware procurement, billing UI changes, and customer-facing API surface.

Why now
-------
- Increasing multi-tenant interference: 30% of P95 tail-latency incidents in 2026 were traced to allocation imbalance or stale cache prefetching decisions.
- Observability fragmentation: multiple dashboards use different cost attributions, causing inconsistent incident triage.
- Product opportunity: enabling predictable tenant burst behaviour unlocks Dedicated capacity contracts and smoother autoscaling.

Principles
----------
1. Single source of truth for placement decisions and allocation metadata.
2. Telemetry-first: allocation events must emit structured telemetry consumed by SLI synthesizer.
3. Operator-first UX: dashboards and alerts should make corrective actions explicit and automatable.
4. Incremental deployability: every milestone is safe to roll back and has a canary validation plan.

High-level timeline and milestones
--------------------------------
| Quarter | Milestone (owner) | Outcome |
|---------|-------------------|---------|
| Q1 2027 | allocation-metadata-spec (allocator, SRE) | Common JSON schema v1, instrumentation hooks defined |
| Q2 2027 | telemetry-fanout refactor (infra) | Low-latency event fanout to SLI synthesizer and operator-buses |
| Q3 2027 | SLI synthesizer MVP + dashboards (observability) | Unified token-latency and token-cost SLIs, root cause tags emitted |
| Q4 2027 | allocator-v2 canary (allocator team) | Canary in 1 region with auto-eviction safety controls |
| Q1 2028 | prefetch-hint integration + automated corrective playbooks | Operator playbooks trigger prefetching or tenant soft-move suggestions |
| Q2 2028 | global rollout + runbook consolidation | Road-tested dashboards and consolidated runbooks published |
| Q3 2028 | operator-surface SDK GA (platform) | SDK to create playbooks and custom adaptive alerts |
| Q4 2028 | KPI review and cost-economics analysis | SLO adherence, incident reduction, and cost delta report |

Milestone acceptance criteria
-----------------------------
- allocation-metadata-spec: schema reviewed by Observability, SRE, Runtime; backwards-compatible fields; example events included.
- telemetry-fanout refactor: 99th percentile fanout latency <200ms for allocation events during synthetic load.
- SLI synthesizer MVP: single dashboard showing aligned P50/P95 latency and per-tenant cost with <5% variance versus baseline reports.
- allocator-v2 canary: no >3% increase in p95 across affected tenants for 72 hours; auto-rollback triggers validated.

Ownership and stakeholders
--------------------------
- Product owner: Priya Rao (product)
- Technical lead (allocator): Liam Chen (eng-platform)
- Observability lead: Sofia Martinez (eng-platform)
- SRE oncall liaison: Alex Rivera (eng-sre)
- Privacy & Compliance: Hannah Gold (security-and-compliance) for telemetry PII checks

SLOs/SLIs and thresholds (impacting platform SLIs)
--------------------------------------------------
- Token-generation latency (short requests, <=128 tokens): p50 < 20ms, p95 < 120ms, error-rate < 0.05%
- Warm-prefix cache hit rate (critical tenants): target 95% for top-100 tenants
- Allocation decision propagation time (from placement event to effective routing): p95 < 2s in steady state
- Fanout event delivery: p99 < 500ms
- Operator MTTD for allocation-induced degradations: target < 6 minutes (improvement from current ~18 min)

Dashboards & Alerts changes
--------------------------
- New dashboards (published templates):
  - Allocation health overview: global allocation headroom, per-region fairness score, prefetch backlog
  - Tenant impact timeline: correlated token-latency, allocation-churn, and KV-cache-miss heatmap
  - Synthetic steady-state lab: canary-run summary graphs and regression deltas

- Alert rules (examples):
  1) Allocation-churn-surge: trigger if allocation-churn-rate > 3x baseline for 5 min AND p95 token-latency increased > 15% 
     - Severity: P2, Notify: allocator-runbook (pager) + post to #allocator-ops slack
  2) Prefetch-failure-spike: if prefetch-failure-rate > 0.5% for 10 min
     - Severity: P3, Annotate incident with last successful prefetch snapshot and run prefetch-diagnostic job
  3) Fanout-latency-degradation: p99 fanout latency > 1s for 2 min
     - Severity: P1, Immediate paging to infra oncall

Operator runbook snippets
------------------------
1. Triage allocation-churn-surge (abridged):
   a) Open allocation dashboard -> identify top affected tenant IDs.
   b) Query: allocation-event stream for tenant <TENANT_ID> (last 15m)
      ```bash
      http --stream GET "https://telemetry.internal/allocation-events?tenant=<TENANT_ID>&since=15m" |
        jq -r '.events[] | {ts: .ts, action: .action, reason: .reason, version: .version}'
      ```
   c) If event shows repeated prefetch evictions, run prefetch-diagnostic job and collect KV prefix traces.
   d) If p95 spike coincides with allocation delta >20% in 10m, escalate to allocator-oncall and run automated soft-move playbook.

2. Automated corrective playbook (high level):
   - Preconditions: canary flag enabled for tenant, health checks passing for target hosts.
   - Actions: trigger prefetch-hint for top-3 prefixes, apply temporary soft-credit to tenant slice, monitor p95 for 15 minutes.
   - Rollback: if p95 does not improve or error-rate increases by >0.3%, undo changes and file incident.

Integration tests and validation
-------------------------------
- Synthetic lab scenarios to validate: cold-cache ramp, tenant burst with interleaved small/large requests, KV-shard node failure.
- Test harness: use the existing predictive-batching simulator with two new modules: allocation-replay and telemetry-asserts. Example config: 
  ```yaml
  scenario: tenant-burst-3x
  tenants: 250
  duration: 15m
  metrics_assert: {
    "p95_token_latency": "<=120ms",
    "fanout_delivery_p99": "<=500ms"
  }
  ```

Rollback criteria and safe-fail modes
------------------------------------
- Canary auto-rollback triggers: >3% regressions in p95 across canary cohort for 1 hour OR any P1 increase in error-rate.
- Safe-fail modes implemented: allocator-v2 has an operator-initiated fallback to allocation-v1 (stateless switch) and an automated gradual throttling policy (soft-credit throttle) to protect shared resources.

Risk assessment and mitigations
------------------------------
- Risk: Telemetry increases cardinality and costs.
  - Mitigation: sample non-critical tenants at 1%, apply dynamic sampling rules and compress event payloads.
- Risk: Misaligned corrective playbooks might worsen tail latency for other tenants.
  - Mitigation: run playbooks in canary tenant pools first, enforce global fairness budget and pre-execution simulation in lab.
- Risk: Operator cognitive overload from new dashboards.
  - Mitigation: publish concise operator cheat-sheets, train the oncall rotation with three gameday scenarios.

Open action items (owners)
-------------------------
- Finalize allocation-metadata-spec v1 (Liam Chen) - due 2026-12-31.
- Prototype SLI synthesizer ingest pipeline (Sofia Martinez) - due 2027-02-28.
- Create dashboard templates and alert playbook drafts (Alex Rivera) - due 2027-04-15.
- Define cost accounting for telemetry egress (Finance) - due 2027-03-01.
